recommendation_text: PPG is weakly recommended for early gastric cancer in the middle portion of the stomach (Consensus rate 100%, 10/10, Strength of evidence C).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for function-preserving surgery/CQ2-2 Is proximal gastrectomy recommended for early proximal gastric cancer as function-preserving surgery?
recommendation_text: Proximal gastrectomy is weakly recommended for early proximal gastric cancer as function-preserving surgery (Consensus rate 90%, 9/10, Strength of evidence C).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for combined resection and extended surgery/CQ3-1 Is omentectomy recommended for advanced gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: Omentectomy is weakly recommended for cT3-T4 gastric cancer (Consensus rate 80%, 8/10, Strength of evidence C).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for combined resection and extended surgery/CQ3-2 Is splenectomy or splenic hilar lymph node dissection recommended for advanced proximal gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: It is strongly recommended not to perform splenectomy or splenic hilar lymph node dissection for tumors which have not invaded the greater curvature (Consensus rate 100%, 9/9, Strength of evidence A).

recommendation_text: Pancreaticoduodenectomy is weakly recommended for advanced gastric cancer with invasion of the duodenum or head of the pancreas with certain conditions (Consensus rate 100%, 10/10, Strength of evidence C).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for appropriate staging/CQ4-1 Is PET-CT recommended for the staging of gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: It is weakly recommended not to perform PET-CT (Consensus rate 70%, 7/10, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for appropriate staging/CQ4-1 Is PET-CT recommended for the staging of gastric cancer?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for appropriate staging/CQ4-2 Is staging laparoscopy recommended for determining the treatment strategy in advanced gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: Staging laparoscopy is weakly recommended to determine the treatment strategy for patients with advanced gastric cancer who are likely to have peritoneal metastasis (Consensus rate 90%, 9/10, Strength of evidence B).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for appropriate staging/CQ4-2 Is staging laparoscopy recommended for determining the treatment strategy in advanced gastric cancer?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for Stage IV gastric cancer/CQ5-1 Is surgical treatment for oligometastases recommended?
recommendation_text: Surgical resection after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is weakly recommended for a small number of paraaortic lymph node metastases confined to No.16a2/b1, if there are no other non-curable factors (Consensus rate 94.7%, 18/19, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for Stage IV gastric cancer/CQ5-1 Is surgical treatment for oligometastases recommended?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for Stage IV gastric cancer/CQ5-3 Is palliative resection, bypass surgery, or stent placement recommended for bleeding or stenosis from incurable gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: Palliative resection, bypass surgery, or stent placement is weakly recommended for bleeding or stenosis from incurable gastric cancer (Consensus rate 100%, 19/19), Strength of evidence D).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for Stage IV gastric cancer/CQ5-3 Is palliative resection, bypass surgery, or stent placement recommended for bleeding or stenosis from incurable gastric cancer?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for esophagogastric junctional cancer/CQ6-1 Is mediastinal lymph node dissection or para-aortic lymph node dissection recommended for the surgery for esophagogastric junctional cancer?
recommendation_text: In surgery for esophagogastric junctional cancer deeper than cT2, Lower mediastinal lymph node dissection is weakly recommended if the esophageal invasion length is greater than 2 cm (Consensus rate 90%, 9/10, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for esophagogastric junctional cancer/CQ6-1 Is mediastinal lymph node dissection or para-aortic lymph node dissection recommended for the surgery for esophagogastric junctional cancer?

recommendation_text: Upper, middle, and lower mediastinal lymph node dissection is weakly recommended if the esophageal invasion length is greater than 4 cm (Consensus rate 80%, 8/10, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for esophagogastric junctional cancer/CQ6-1 Is mediastinal lymph node dissection or para-aortic lymph node dissection recommended for the surgery for esophagogastric junctional cancer?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for esophagogastric junctional cancer/CQ6-1 Is mediastinal lymph node dissection or para-aortic lymph node dissection recommended for the surgery for esophagogastric junctional cancer?
recommendation_text: It is weakly recommended not to perform para-aortic lymph node (No.16a2) dissection, taking into consideration the entire surgical stress (Consensus rate 100%, 10/10, Strength of evidence C).

recommendation_text: Laparoscopic or robotic surgery is weakly recommended for esophagogastric junctional cancer (Consensus rate 70%, 7/10, Strength of evidence D).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for elderly patients/CQ10-1 Is considering age recommended when deciding a surgical procedure?
recommendation_text: Limited surgery with reduced lymph node dissection or minimally invasive surgery is weakly recommended for elderly patients (Consensus rate 100%, 19/19, Strength of evidence D).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for elderly patients/CQ10-2 Is considering age recommended when deciding on the indication for systemic chemotherapy?
recommendation_text: Considering age when deciding on the indication of systemic chemotherapy is weakly recommended for an elderly patient with unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer, who is fit, has decision-making capacity, and is willing to undergo treatment after carefully assessing the patient’s overall condition and motivation (Consensus rate 100%, 19/19, Strength of evidence B).

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ11-1 Is chemotherapy recommended for patients with impaired oral intake or massive ascites due to extensive peritoneal disease?
recommendation_text: Chemotherapy is weakly recommended for patients with impaired oral intake or massive ascites after careful assessment of their general condition (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ11-1 Is chemotherapy recommended for patients with impaired oral intake or massive ascites due to extensive peritoneal disease?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ11-2 Is personalized medicine based on genomic profiling tests recommended for AGC?
recommendation_text: It is weakly recommended to perform appropriate genomic profiling tests in later-line treatment and to treat based on the genetic alterations found for unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer patients (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ12 Are immune checkpoint inhibitors recommended for first-line treatment of HER2-negative AGC?
recommendation_text: Chemotherapy in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) is strongly recommended as first-line treatment for HER2-negative unresectable advanced/recurrent gastric/gastroesophageal junction cancer, taking into account biomarkers (PD-L1 (CPS), MSI, MMR, CLDN18) and the patient’s general condition (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence A).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ12 Are immune checkpoint inhibitors recommended for first-line treatment of HER2-negative AGC?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ13-1 Is selection of first-line treatment based on biomarkers recommended?
recommendation_text: Selection of first-line treatment based on biomarkers is strongly recommended for patients with unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence A).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ13-1 Is selection of first-line treatment based on biomarkers recommended?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ14 After progression of chemotherapy for unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer, is it recommended to continue or re-administer drugs used in previous treatment?
recommendation_text: It is strongly recommended not to continuously use or re-administer fluoropyrimidine, trastuzumab, or ramucirumab in chemotherapy for unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancers (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence A).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for chemotherapy/CQ14 After progression of chemotherapy for unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer, is it recommended to continue or re-administer drugs used in previous treatment?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for palliative care/CQ15-1 Is anamorelin recommended for cachexic patients?
recommendation_text: In patients with advanced gastric cancer and a non-refractory cachexia state, appropriate dosing of anamorelin is weakly recommended to promote appetite and weight gain (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence D).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for palliative care/CQ15-1 Is anamorelin recommended for cachexic patients?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for palliative care/CQ15-2 Is radiation recommended as palliative treatment for bleeding advanced gastric cancer?
recommendation_text: For patients with incurable advanced gastric cancer with bleeding, radiation for the purpose of hemostasis is weakly recommended, taking into consideration the patient’s overall condition and prognosis (Consensus rate 100%, 7/7, Strength of evidence C).
source_name: Japanese gastric cancer treatment guidelines 2025 (7th edition)
source_section: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for palliative care/CQ15-2 Is radiation recommended as palliative treatment for bleeding advanced gastric cancer?

breadcrumb: Clinical questions for surgery (Table 5)/Clinical questions for perioperative chemotherapy/CQ16-2 Is adjuvant chemotherapy recommended for stage IV gastric cancer with R0 resection?
recommendation_text: Adjuvant chemotherapy is weakly recommended for stage IV gastric cancer with R0 resection (Consensus rate 94.7%, 18/19, Strength of evidence C).
